title: Bits, bytes, characters, and pixels

spans.caption: A diagram of the lesson’s key ideas

spans.text: A bit is the smallest unit of computer data and has a value of 0 or 1. A byte is 8 bits. Lowercase `b` often means bit and uppercase `B` means byte; network speed may use Mbit/s while file size uses MB.
Divide bits by 8 to get bytes; multiply bytes by 8 to get bits. For example, 24 bits = 3 bytes and 5 bytes = 40 bits. Decimal 1 kB = 1000 bytes; binary 1 KiB = 1024 bytes. Do not mix up kB and KiB.
How many bytes is a character?

It depends on the character and encoding. In UTF-8, `A` takes 1 byte and `é` takes 2 bytes. Many emoji take 4 bytes; a displayed symbol made by combining characters can use more because it contains multiple Unicode code points. There is no rule that one character always equals one byte.
How many bytes is a pixel?
A pixel’s size depends on color depth. An uncompressed RGB pixel is commonly 24 bits, or 3 bytes; RGBA with a transparency channel is 32 bits, or 4 bytes. Other color formats can differ.

A 1920 × 1080 RGB image has 1920 × 1080 × 3 = 6,220,800 raw bytes, about 5.93 MiB. This is the uncompressed pixel data only. PNG/JPEG compression, file headers, color format, and row padding change the actual file size.
